summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 7.9). Installed aide 0.15.1 from CentOS vault (no subscription-manager repos were enabled), configured /etc/aide.conf to scope FULL (permissions/inode/owner/group/size/mtime/ctime/acl/selinux/xattrs/md5+sha256) monitoring to /etc, initialized and activated the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, added a weekly cron job (/etc/cron.d/aide-check) for ongoing checks, and validated detection works via a reversible add/remove test. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, triggered a native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified the AIDE database and config survived and correctly detected a legitimate post-boot change (/etc/resolv.conf regenerated by DHCP), then refreshed the baseline to the current clean state (final check: 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!').
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/tooling and repo availability
Downloaded and installed aide-0.15.1-13.el7 RPM from CentOS vault (no RHEL subscription repos enabled)
Backed up /etc/aide.conf to /etc/aide.conf.orig and wrote a new /etc/aide.conf scoping FULL rule (p+i+n+u+g+s+m+c+acl+selinux+xattrs+md5+sha256) to /etc with sane exclusions
Initialized AIDE database and activated it as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
Ran aide --check to confirm a clean baseline (exit 0)
Performed reversible functional test: added /etc/aide-selftest-marker.txt, confirmed AIDE flagged it as 'added', removed it, confirmed AIDE flagged the resulting /etc directory mtime change
Re-initialized the baseline to reflect the clean post-test state and confirmed clean check
Captured pre-restart boot_id and AIDE db hash as health baseline
Triggered node1 reboot via 'shutdown -r now', acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed changed boot_id and current uptime
Verified aide package, database file, cron job, and crond service all persisted through restart
Ran aide --check post-restart, confirming it correctly detected a legitimate DHCP-driven change to /etc/resolv.conf, proving the baseline is functional post-reboot
Refreshed the baseline once more to the current known-good post-reboot state and confirmed a final clean check

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and integrity baseline for /etc initialized and activated
evidence.summary: Installed aide-0.15.1-13.el7, wrote /etc-scoped aide.conf, initialized /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and confirmed initial clean check ('All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!')

evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly detects changes to /etc (functional proof, not just config)
evidence.summary: Reversible test: added /etc/aide-selftest-marker.txt -> AIDE reported 'added: /etc/aide-selftest-marker.txt'; removed it -> AIDE reported the resulting /etc directory mtime/ctime change

evidence.requirement: Baseline refreshed to a clean, known-good final state before restart
evidence.summary: Re-initialized and reactivated the database after the self-test; final check exit 0, 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!', hash e61c57f8...

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health) on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf, confirmed AIDE db present with hash e61c57f8..., pre-restart check clean, cron job present
'sudo shutdown -r now' launched in background with disown; exec call returned 'reboot-triggered' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node became unreachable during restart, then came back with a changed boot identity
evidence.summary: SSH connection timed out during reboot; subsequent poll succeeded with boot_id 9655a8b7-a398-46d2-8b43-0bd3d5aa9783 (changed from e9250ad1...) and new uptime, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of integrity baseline data/service and cluster-relevant state
evidence.summary: Post-restart: aide package present, database file persisted with unchanged hash, cron job intact; aide --check correctly detected legitimate post-boot resolv.conf regeneration, then baseline was refreshed and final check returned clean ('All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!')
